gaps.sentence: The instructions were unclear, so I had to ___ them completely (WRITE).
gaps.hint: write again — unclear the first time (re-); base verb needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again: rewrite. A base verb is needed after 'had to'.

gaps.sentence: It is almost ___ to park in the city centre (POSSIBLE).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed — parking is extremely difficult
gaps.explanation: The in- of 'possible' becomes im- before p: impossible. The context shows a negative meaning.

gaps.sentence: His ___ (BEHAVE) at school has improved enormously.
The company is a major ___ (EMPLOY) in the region.
gaps.hint: the company gives jobs — it is the one who employs
gaps.explanation: An employer gives work; an employee receives it. The sentence is about the company.

gaps.sentence: The thunderstorm was absolutely ___ , so the children hid under the blankets (TERRIFY).
gaps.hint: the storm causes the fear (-ing); note 'terrific' means excellent
gaps.explanation: The storm causes terror, so it is terrifying; the children felt terrified. 'Terrific' means excellent.

gaps.sentence: We had a ___ view of the coast from the plane (SPECTACLE).
gaps.explanation: The adjective of 'spectacle' is spectacular; it modifies the noun 'view'.

gaps.sentence: The island is ___ , with no permanent residents (HABIT).
gaps.explanation: 'No permanent residents' shows the negative: uninhabited (un- + inhabited). An adjective is needed after 'is'.

gaps.sentence: It is ___ to smoke inside public buildings (LEGAL).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: against the law (il-)
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'legal' is 'illegal' (il- before l). An adjective is needed after 'is'.
